attributes.function: trains, certifies and holds the seals of surveyors; keeps the master level and the reference brines
attributes.house_rule: a level is a level and the ground does not care who owns it; a finding is entered on the College roll before it is shown to the body that commissioned it
attributes.instruments: the water-glass, the chain, the master level at the far rim
attributes.relationship_to_wardens: the Wardenry cannot lawfully survey without College-sealed surveyors, and the College cannot reach the plain without the Wardenry's licences. Neither can do without the other and neither likes it.
attributes.seat: the far rim, opposite Bell Harrow
attributes.weakness: no money, no wagons, no enforcement — it can prove a thing to the last decimal and do absolutely nothing about it

name: The College of Levels
summary: The chartered surveyors' college on the far rim, which trains and seals every person permitted to set an instrument on the Meniscus and put a number to what they see. It certifies the Wardenry's surveyors but does not employ them, so a Warden-surveyor carries two loyalties and one seal. Its house rule — that findings are entered on the roll before they are shown to anyone — is the reason a copy of the water survey exists eight hundred miles from the packet.
